newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil central banker Lopes to stay on board.
newsitem.headline: Brazil central banker Lopes to stay on board.

text.p: The Director of Monetary Policy at Brazil's Central Bank, Francisco "Chico" Lopes, sees no reason to leave the bank following the resignation of its head, Gustavo Loyola.

In an interview with O Globo newspaper published Thursday, Lopes said he had always worked well with Gustavo Franco, the bank's Director of International Affairs who has been nominated to take over the presidency from Loyola.
"I've always worked with this team and would have no reasons to leave. Everything will continue as it has before in economic policy," Lopes told O Globo.
Lopes also praised the choice of Franco, saying he was well suited to the job of Central Bank president.

The Central Bank said Wednesday that Director of Controls Alkimar Moura would follow Loyola's lead and resign. Moura's exit had been agreed a long time ago, the bank said, and was not directly related to the changes in the boardroom.

On Wednesday, rumors began to circulate in Brasilia and in the markets that Lopes too might resign. Lopes has long been identified as Franco's opposite, more an advocate of looser monetary policy than his colleague.
But Globo said Lopes had denied there were any policy disagreements between the two. Such speculation was a media product and nothing else, he said.
Successors to Franco and Moura are expected to be announced Friday.
